$comment: Declared versions NOT published from this repository, each with the reason.
State is computed from this repository's git tags. a1 and a2 were published
from dotmac_starter_mt and their tags stay there permanently.
EMPTY, and that is the correct state: every declared version is published.
0.1.0a3 is published and permanently unpinnable; 0.1.0a4 is published,
independently verified, and refused for adoption; 0.1.0a5 is published,
verified on seven properties, and refused for adoption because its declared
dotmac-kernel floor is 21 alphas below the module it imports; 0.1.0a6 is
published, verified, and still pinnable; 0.1.0a7 is published, verified on
seven properties with nine behavioural canaries, publishes mod_deploy's
exact seven-table, 95-column structure, declares >=0.1.0a100, and is the
version to pin. All of them live in docs/published-versions.json, each
superseding disposition APPENDED to its original record rather than
replacing it.
The a7 row that sat here between the declaration and the publication is
gone in the change that records the coordinates — the discipline a5 and a6
kept and the a4 row failed by six hours. a7 came close to failing it the
same way: the row outlived its own publication and verification, and while
it did, test_the_declared_version_is_accounted_for failed on main state, so
every pull request opened in that window went red, including an empty one.
The gate saw the contradiction this time — the checkout fetches tags now,
which is the half the a4 defect fixed. What has still not been automated is
the follow-up itself; the verify run only prints `##[notice]OWED`.
A row here and a row in docs/published-versions.json are never both true
about one version at once, and
test_the_ledger_and_the_published_record_never_claim_the_same_version states
that over the two FILES so it holds even in a tagless checkout.
